Definition: from G1 (as negative particle) and G1075; unregistered as to birth:--without descent.
BiblicalUsage: Agenealogetos means 'without descent' — unregistered, with no genealogy on record — and it appears once, of Melchizedek: 'Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life.' The writer is not saying Melchizedek had no parents; he is saying Scripture records none, and that silence makes him a fitting picture of the Son of God, whose priesthood has no end.
TheologicalSignificance: Melchizedek arrives without a genealogy, and this word only marks the absence — the mystery belongs to the priest, not to the adjective.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
